🐾 Here’s the story behind Matt’s payments work at **JP Morgan Chase**.

From **August 2009 to June 2012**, Matt served as Technology Delivery Lead for ACCESS Next Generation, the bank’s unified corporate banking portal. The challenge was more than replacing a user interface: regional payment systems had different data models, connectivity, entitlements, and regulatory requirements. Bottomline Technologies’ WebSeries platform provided the foundation, but the bank needed payment capabilities beyond its out-of-box offering.

Matt managed a blended team of **40+** **Accenture** and bank resources across Mumbai, Bangalore, and the US. He spent **70 to 80%** of his time embedded at Bottomline’s Portsmouth offices, working through where native platform capabilities ended and bespoke engineering was required.

He designed and delivered ACH, wire, FX/cross-border, and tax payment modules, each with distinct validation, formatting, settlement, and compliance requirements. He also built payment verification through Message Authentication Codes and payment-type-specific permissions, such as allowing wire approval without allowing FX initiation. For the global payments gateway, he designed message transformation, protocol translation, and routing across **12 countries**, connecting ACCESS to clearing networks and internal compliance, settlement, and reporting systems.

Rather than retain individual permission configuration, Matt introduced role-based profiles and bulk changes across users, accounts, and products. Entitlement management fell from days to minutes. He also led legacy payment-data migration without disruption to live payment operations, preserving client configurations, transaction histories, and compliance traceability.

For regional rollout, Matt translated local regulatory requirements into data-visibility and access controls, sequencing launches by regulatory readiness rather than using a single global deployment. He also owned production incident response and cross-team root-cause analysis.

ACCESS launched in **April 2011**, consolidating regional systems into a single portal serving **135,000+** corporate, financial institution, government, and municipal clients across **180+ countries**.

Matt’s work spans Execution & Delivery, Org & Working-Model Transformation, and Talent & Enablement: enterprise platforms, new engineering organizations, and practices that client teams continued using after engagements ended. His career progressed from software engineer to solution architect to director and Cloud Innovation Center leader.

At **Accenture**, clients were struggling with slow development cycles, fragmented workflows, and legacy systems. They wanted to move beyond waterfall delivery and feature factories, but practices such as pair programming and test-driven development needed to work within enterprise security, compliance, and governance requirements.

Matt built the Atlanta and Tampa Cloud Innovation Centers from **0 to 150+ practitioners**, owning full P&L accountability. He brought product managers, designers, and engineers together in balanced teams, adapted Lean XP for enterprise complexity, and created reusable playbooks. Instead of presenting methodology through slides alone, he invited clients to observe standups, pairing, and teams working through problems together at whiteboards.

At **Capital One**, slow iterations and misaligned priorities were extending time-to-market. Matt introduced a client-prioritized, testable backlog, thin-slice MVPs, and disciplined red-green-refactor practice. The team delivered features **3 to 4 times faster** than other **Accenture** teams on the same engagement, with **zero production defects**. The client sought to retain the team beyond the planned engagement.

He also built the training behind that delivery: tailored onboarding, mentoring, and an “I do, we do, you do” learning model. Practitioners progressed from guided to independent delivery, with near-zero attrition during the first **two years**.

Across the centers, teams delivered **30+ product engagements** for **15+ Fortune 500 clients**, contributing to **\$100M+ in repeat business** through delivery excellence and customer relationships.

answer_md:
🐾 Here’s how Matt built AWS Launchpad.

At **Accenture’s** Liquid Studio, traditional training programs weren’t keeping pace with rapidly evolving AWS technologies. Engineers had gaps in cloud competency, and cloud adoption was slowing. The Atlanta Innovation Hub needed a structured program that would help engineers earn certifications and prepare them to lead cloud-native transformation initiatives.

From **July 2018** to **November 2019**, Matt led AWS Launchpad as Cloud Native Architecture Lead. The program was developed in collaboration with AWS. Rather than relying on theory alone, he combined structured learning paths, hands-on labs, and mentor-based training.

Matt designed learning paths and certification programs covering AWS core services, including Lambda, API Gateway, DynamoDB, Kubernetes, and ECS/Fargate, alongside cloud-native application development. He delivered interactive workshops and labs that immersed engineers in real-world AWS environments, reinforcing practical application over theory.

He also established cloud expert mentorship teams so engineers could learn AWS best practices from experienced practitioners. Group coaching sessions and knowledge-sharing workshops gave participants additional ways to work through the material and share knowledge. The program paired certification preparation with practical cloud work, rather than treating the exam as the only goal.

More than **200 professionals earned AWS certifications**, including AWS Solutions Architect and DevOps Engineer certifications. The program accelerated cloud adoption and the launch of cloud-native initiatives at **Accenture**, while establishing ongoing learning and capability-building across teams.
